summary: Re-review of r2 (audio-r2-tech/music.json) against status 'Fix round 2', all measured in the browser. Verified fixed: TB, the boot without WebAudio: with AudioContext/OfflineAudioContext deleted the game boots, menu and race work, 0 errors; a rejected 32 kHz rate falls back to 48 kHz and plays. TR, the race-start sync, measured against the REAL GO event on mountain: first race 0 ms, pause 1.5 s in the intro -8 ms, pause 1.2 s at '1' -4 ms, pause -> 重新开始 +8 ms, 3 rapid restarts -8 ms; no section A while paused; the crossfade list empties. t4 WebKit: the context is 'suspended' before the gesture and running after it. t1 mute, t2 voice pause, t3 trace: the unit's checks are green. T5: system.ts is 378 lines, with pump, barks and trace split out. B1 (music blocker): the env.ts retrigger renders 0 before a reused-voice note with no step > 0.011, and the offline regression (22 instruments + 8 stingers) is green. Other checks: tsc 0 errors; no any, ts-ignore, empty catch or Math.random in the unit; largest file 378 lines; 0 __br.errors and 0 console warnings over 3 consecutive 1080p races. No leaks: live WebAudio nodes after GC 196/194/197 (179 back in the menu); heap 37.4/39.1/39.6 MB against 35.4/36.7/37.5 with ?stub=audio, the same drift, so not audio. Performance: 121-122 fps, 257 draw calls, 0.90 M triangles, identical with ?stub=audio. Gameplay is bit-identical with the audio unit, with ?stub=audio and run to run. A race quit, restarted or paused mid-KO-cinematic leaves muffle 0, hit duck 1 and no bass drop, with music audible. Events reach their sound in 0.2-4.5 ms; node churn is 23/s in the menu, 71/s in a race, 87/s in the stretch. Not passing. (1) The audio thread is still over the brief's 5 % CPU bar in every race measurement: the soundtrack alone costs 4.2-4.4 % (6.6 % in the final stretch), and the unit's CPU gate cannot fail on this machine. (2) A real bark-priority bug drops the player's KO quip after cinematics, and it makes the unit's own audio-check exit 1. Minor: the CPU gate's pack burst uses a non-existent weapon; race still calls sfx() for police sounds (cross-unit); a misleading warning on the no-WebAudio path. Evidence: shots/review/audio/r3-tech/ (audio-check.log, probe-*.json/.mjs, contact-1.jpg).

issues.title: Audio thread still over the 5 % CPU budget in every race measurement (r2 C1 only partly fixed); the soundtrack alone uses 4.2-6.6 %
issues.detail: Method: CDP WebAudio.getRealtimeData renderCapacity at 1920x1080, machine load 8-18 on 10 cores. A one-oscillator 32 kHz control context in a second page of the same browser read 0.34-0.43 % throughout, so load does not inflate the meter. Music alone, no session (probe-cpu-idle.json): race-coast 4.16 % p50 / 6.07 % p90, race-city 4.30 / 5.15, race-mountain 4.42 / 8.16, final-stretch layer 6.55 / 8.56; idle engine 0.84 / 1.97. Full autopilot race, 5 samples (probe-cpu-a.json, probe-cpu-b.json, probe-races-coast.json): p50 5.21-7.24 % (over 5 % in 5/5), p90 6.48-12.34 % (over the unit's own 8 % in 3/5). Other phases: busy pack 6.88-9.33 / 10.3-14.66; stretch 6.39-7.29 / 8.04-9.79; sfx + bike loops only 1.8-2.4 / 3.7-5.2. This is about 40 % better than r2 (race p50 9-13 %), but the music by itself already uses the whole budget. The offline cpuNet the status quotes (race-coast 1.42 %) under-reports the realtime cost by about 3x. The gate does not enforce anything: tools/audio-check-cpu.mjs turns every overrun into 'warn' when load > 0.6 x cores, which is always true on this shared machine. My full run at load 29 read race 8.3/11.1, pack 9.6/15.4, stretch 9.1/15.3, all 'warn'.
issues.fix: Make the music mostly buffer playback, as already done for keys and drums. Render brass stabs/swells per voicing and pad chords per section once (OfflineAudioContext + LRU like the Rhodes chord cache). Sample the slap bass per pitch x articulation (thumb/pop/dead/slide) and the leads per 3-semitone zone, played with playbackRate, so a note = 1 source + 1 gain. Build the top-3/stretch layer voices only while engaged. Make the gate real: normalise against a control context, or wait/retry until load < 0.6 x cores and FAIL if menu/race/pack/stretch never get under p50 5 % / p90 8 %. Record the result in status.

issues.title: VoicePlayer.cut() keeps the cut line's busy time, so the player's KO quip (and the victim's line) is dropped after cinematics and the unit's own audio-check exits 1
issues.detail: src/audio/voice/player.ts:166-174: cut() fades the line and clears current[channel] but leaves busy[channel] at the cut clip's original end. start() of a LOUD announcer line (:157-161) then takes Math.max(busy.bark, ...), so the silenced bark still counts, and play() (:104) drops every bark until busy.bark + BARK_GAP. probe-quip.json, KO #3: sloth_taunt_3 (2.39 s) started 0.92 s before __br.ko. ann_ko cut it at the peak (audio t 33.54) but busy.bark stayed 34.562. At cine:ko end (34.388) pelican_ko_0 -> 'dropped' and capybara_hurt_0 -> 'dropped': silence where the design (events-combat.ts:49-56) promises the pelican's quip. This happened in 1 of 4 KOs. In my full `node tools/audio-check.mjs` run, the same cause gave 'FAIL player KO -> the pelican's own quip after the cinematic (seagull_taunt_0)' and exit 1 (audio-check.log). The acceptance gate is red again. setPaused(true) -> cut('bark') has the same effect: barks stay blocked after resume.
issues.fix: In cut(), set busy[channel] = Math.min(busy[channel], now + 0.07) (the end of the fade), so the gap counts from when the line really stopped. Give the KO lines held for the cinematic end a priority that pre-empts a rival bark, or let them bypass BARK_GAP. Add an audio-check-game case: start a long rival bark (e.g. sloth_taunt_3) 0.5 s before __br.ko(victim, 0) and assert pelican_ko_* is traced after cine:ko end.

issues.title: The CPU gate's pack burst emits a weapon that does not exist ('fish'), so the busiest case is under-measured
issues.detail: tools/audio-check-cpu.mjs:36 packBurst cycles weapons ['fish', 'pan', ...], but WeaponId is 'saltfish'. Every 6th combat:hit maps to 'hit.fish', which SfxPlayer rejects as unknown (warning, returns 0). So 1/6 of the burst's hits are silent and the 'pack' number the status quotes is low. My corrected burst (probe-cpu.mjs, 'saltfish') read pack p50 6.88-9.33 % / p90 10.3-14.66 %.
issues.fix: Use 'saltfish' (better: import the weapon ids from src/data/weapons.ts), and fail the gate on any '[audio] unknown sfx' warning logged during it.

issues.title: cross-unit: race/police.ts still calls app.audio.sfx() directly for the police horn, whistle and corgi knocks
issues.detail: src/gameplay/race/police.ts:127 sfx('traffic.horn.police'), :144 sfx('police.whistle'), :157 sfx(<knock>). These play centred at full volume wherever the corgi is, bypassing audio's placement, air absorption and rate limits. The audio unit's core request (police:whistle event) is still pending.
issues.fix: Core adds 'police:whistle': { riderId, pos } and race emits it (knocks via combat:hit). audio then places them like every other world sound, and race drops the direct sfx() calls.

issues.title: The no-WebAudio path logs a misleading '32 kHz context unavailable, using the device rate' warning before the real one
issues.detail: src/audio/system.ts:46-52: createContext() retries without sampleRate on ANY error, including 'AudioContext is not defined'. probe-robust.json ('none'): the log shows '[audio] 32 kHz context unavailable, using the device rate ReferenceError: AudioContext is not defined', then '[audio] WebAudio unavailable...'. The first message is wrong and confuses triage. Behaviour is otherwise correct.
issues.fix: Throw straight away when typeof AudioContext === 'undefined', and retry without sampleRate only for a NotSupportedError.
